title: Model Weight Fingerprinting: Can Stolen Weights Be Identified After Exfiltration?

original_idea.body:
# Model Weight Fingerprinting: Can Stolen Weights Be Identified After Exfiltration?

**Problem:** OpenAI identifies model weight theft as making all alignment work moot. If weights are stolen, the ability to detect and attribute the theft could deter future attacks and enable response.

**Direction:** Survey watermarking and fingerprinting techniques for neural network weights (steganographic watermarks, functional fingerprints). Test whether a simple weight fingerprint survives fine-tuning on open-source models. Measure detection reliability after various post-theft transformations.

**Why it matters:** If weight fingerprinting is robust to fine-tuning, it provides a deterrence mechanism — stolen weights could be traced back to their source, complicating the attacker's position.

**Relevant context:** OpenAI 2026 Cyber Resilience report; model weight theft as proliferation risk; neural network watermarking literature.
